source.title: Quantifying the Memorization-to-Generalization Transition: Scaling Laws and Phase Structure in Grokking

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some table and figure text is flattened or garbled, so ambiguous per-configuration values are not assigned.
record.tranche_reason: It trains networks on modular arithmetic and measures delayed test generalization after training-set memorization, directly testing algorithmic grokking while sweeping training configurations.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own modular-arithmetic accuracy, timing, weight-decay, and norm results. Claims about Fourier circuits and prior mechanistic findings are cited background or predictions, not results of this study, so they are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains MLPs on modular addition and division and measures when test accuracy passes 95% after training accuracy passes 99%. It sweeps data fraction and weight decay. These are its own results on delayed generalization (V1) and on weight decay's role (V5). It is not one of the original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that data fraction (D^−2.04) and weight decay dominate grokking onset time, with width mattering little. They report a sharp weight-decay boundary near λ≈1.0, below which they say generalization is suppressed. They present norm compression as a regime indicator consistent with implicit regularization. The phase boundary and norm-threshold mechanisms are stated as conjectures, and the limitation to modular-arithmetic MLPs is acknowledged.
record.recipe_differences: Uses modular arithmetic and delayed train-to-test generalization as in the original grokking setup, but studies two tasks with a two-hidden-layer ReLU MLP and learned embeddings, AdamW, and a broad sweep over data fraction, width, learning rate, and weight decay.
record.method_sensitivity: Grokking onset and occurrence vary with data fraction, width, learning rate, and weight decay; grokking is nearly universal at λ ≥ 1.0 but fewer than 60% of configurations grok at λ = 0.1. The delay decreases by more than an order of magnitude as λ increases from 0.1 to 3.0. The D exponent is also reported across multiple test-accuracy thresholds.

fits_no_version.finding: Width has a weak effect on onset time (H^−0.27), far smaller than data fraction. Learning rate scales as η^−0.50, and there are significant pairwise interactions. Wider models grok in fewer steps but at higher FLOP cost.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking onset time follows a power law in hyperparameters, in which data fraction dominates model width.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: Most configurations use a single random seed; 28 runs diverged at high learning rate and low weight decay. The norm analysis covers only 20 configurations, with 14 having a non-trivial gap. The experiments use two modular-arithmetic tasks and MLPs only. The base scaling fit has R2 = 0.732, and the authors say the phase boundary is empirical rather than derived. Some flattened heatmap values cannot be assigned unambiguously.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately assignable results omitted. Per-cell grokking rates in the flattened Figure 6 text are ambiguous and were not attributed to specific conditions.

untested.parts: Chance-level test accuracy before the jump, and the abruptness of the jump. Tasks beyond modular addition and division, and architectures other than MLPs. Dependence of the gap ΔT (rather than onset Tgrok) on training-set size.
Any comparison of the efficiency of generalizing vs memorizing circuits. A critical dataset size, and ungrokking below it. The critical value found here is in weight decay, not data size.
Not tested. Fourier-circuit statements are cited from prior work or offered as predictions.
Not tested: no non-algorithmic data and no initialization-scale manipulation.
Not tested. AdamW is the only optimizer, and there are no numerical-precision controls.

missing.what: Figure 7c/7d correlations: norm at Tmem vs Tgrok labelled ρ=0.63 (p=0.003), and norm change vs gap ρ=0.09 (p=0.759). Both conflict with text claims.
Per-cell grokking rates by width, task, η and λ. Some λ=3.0 high-η cells appear to be 0–50%.
Weibull accelerated failure time fit to all 356 runs (59 censored), concordance 0.71, shape k=1.4. Bears on how abruptly the transition accelerates.
Seed-variance reruns: 10 configurations × 5 seeds, median CV 8%, max 18% near the boundary. One fast configuration grokked in only 4 of 5 seeds.

record.verdict_notes: The paper has internal inconsistencies. Text ρ=0.06 vs figure ρ=0.63 for norm at Tmem. The 'compression rate predicts' claim appears in the text but is a prediction in Appendix D, and Figure 7d gives ρ=0.09. Figure 2 shows 'R² = nan' and Figure 3 shows trivial R²=1.000 FLOPs fits. The 'structurally suppressed' boundary claim is stronger than the data show (λ=0.1 still yields up to ~60% grokking; only 150K steps tested). Most configurations use a single seed. The study is single-author and dated 2026.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures onset at a >95% test-accuracy threshold and reports scaling across data fractions, but does not establish a general chance-to-near-perfect trajectory across other algorithmic tasks or architectures.
It does not track the formation of a generalizing circuit, removal of memorizing components, or a continuous circuit-level progress measure. Fourier-circuit statements are attributed to prior work.
It does not test non-algorithmic data or initialization-scale and lazy-to-rich transitions.
It does not study LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.
It varies weight decay and measures norm compression, but does not compare the efficiency of generalizing and memorizing circuits or test a critical dataset size and ungrokking below it.
It does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
It does not test whether adaptive-optimizer or floating-point artifacts cause the delay or disappear when controlled.

rows.subject: two-hidden-layer MLP with learned embeddings
rows.operation_detail: Sweep of training data fraction, learning rate, weight decay, and width; fit a log-linear model to generalization onset time
rows.measure: Generalization onset time Tgrok; fitted power-law exponents
rows.value: Tgrok ∝ H −0.27 D−2.04 η −0.50 λ−0.64; R2 = 0.732. With interactions, R2 = 0.821.
rows.uncertainty: Exponent standard errors: H ±0.10, D ±0.12, η ±0.04, λ ±0.05.
rows.note: The study reports the pooled fit across the two tasks and 297 grokked runs.
rows.check: Only the D exponent (−2.04 ± 0.12) bears on V1. The H, η and λ exponents do not. The fit models Tgrok, not the gap ΔT, so 'delay grows as data shrinks' is shown for onset time rather than for the post-memorization delay. Figure 2's companion panel prints 'Power law (R² = nan)', an internal glitch.

rows.operation_detail: Count runs meeting the study's grokking definition

conditions.value: Tmem: first step with training accuracy >99%; Tgrok: first step with test accuracy >95%

rows.measure: Runs that grokked within the training budget
rows.note: The study defines a run as non-grokking if Tgrok > 150,000.
rows.check: 'Grokked' means test accuracy >95% within 150K steps, not a delayed transition. In the norm sample only 14 of 20 runs had a non-trivial gap, so this count overstates delayed generalization. About 17% of completed runs never generalized, and 28 further runs diverged.

rows.subject: two-hidden-layer MLP with learned embeddings
rows.operation_detail: Sweep weight decay and learning rate; report fraction of configurations that grokked
rows.value: Nearly all configurations grok regardless of learning rate; the figure text says the rate approaches 100% for λ ≥ 1.0.
rows.note: The paper describes the boundary in aggregate; the flattened heatmap values are not reliably assignable to individual conditions.
rows.check: This is an aggregate statement. The garbled Figure 6 heatmap seems to show 0–50% grokking in some λ=3.0 cells at the highest learning rates. That would qualify 'nearly all grok regardless of η' but cannot be reliably assigned to conditions.

source_check.problem: The prose supports the aggregate claim; flattened Figure 6 cells cannot reliably verify its learning-rate qualification.

rows.subject: two-hidden-layer MLP with learned embeddings
rows.operation_detail: Sweep weight decay and learning rate; report fraction of configurations that grokked
rows.note: The paper says grokking is also sensitive to learning rate at this weight decay.
rows.check: For V5 the state should be observed, not partial: less grokking at low weight decay is what a low-norm-bias account predicts. For V1 it shows that delayed generalization fails in many low-λ runs. The authors call grokking 'structurally suppressed' below λ≈1, yet up to ~60% still grok at λ=0.1 and ~100% at λ=0.3, so the boundary is soft.

source_check.correct: V5: observed; V1: partial within the 150K-step budget, with fewer than 60% crossing the generalization threshold at λ=0.1.
source_check.problem: The shared observed state fits V5 but not the incomplete occurrence of V1 in this condition group.

conditions.value: 20 configurations; 14 had a non-trivial grokking gap

rows.baseline: 1.0 at Tmem by the ratio definition
rows.value: Median 0.42; IQR 0.31–0.54; norm at generalization was lower than at memorization in all 14 runs
rows.note: The paper also reports monotonic compression during the memorization phase in all 14 runs.
rows.check: The sample is small (14 runs). It shows norm compression coinciding with generalization, which is correlational and does not compare circuit efficiency.

source_check.problem: Norm compression is correlational evidence; circuit efficiency was not measured.

rows.operation_detail: Measure association between norm at memorization and generalization onset time
rows.measure: Spearman correlation between absolute norm at Tmem and Tgrok
rows.note: The authors state that absolute norm at Tmem does not predict Tgrok.
rows.check: V5 makes no claim that starting norm predicts onset, so this row bears on no version. The value also conflicts with the Figure 7c panel label, which reads ρ = 0.63 (p = 0.003).

rows.subject: two-hidden-layer MLP with learned embeddings
rows.operation_detail: Relate rate of norm decrease to generalization onset
rows.measure: Association between faster norm compression and earlier grokking
rows.value: Configurations with faster compression grok sooner
rows.note: A numerical correlation for compression rate is not reported.
rows.check: No number supports this text claim. Appendix D lists 'compression rate predicts Tgrok' as a prediction (|ρ|>0.5 predicted), implying it was not measured. Figure 7d shows norm change vs grokking gap at ρ = 0.09 (p = 0.759), which contradicts the text.

relationships.condition: Modular addition mod 113 and division mod 97, 2-layer MLPs, AdamW, grokking runs at 85–99% thresholds
relationships.reason: Gaps reach up to over 100,000 steps after training saturation (r8). Onset time scales roughly as D^−2 across tasks and thresholds (r1–r6). Measured on Tgrok rather than ΔT.
relationships.display_finding: Generalization gaps exceeded 100,000 steps after training saturation, while onset time scaled roughly as dataset size to the power −2 across tasks and thresholds, rather than directly measuring the post-memorization delay.

source_check.reason: r10 reports fewer than 60% generalizing at λ=0.1; r7 reports incomplete generalization overall. This qualifies occurrence within the budget, without establishing permanent failure.

relationships.condition: Weight-decay sweep λ 0.1–3.0 in modular-arithmetic MLPs with AdamW
relationships.reason: Higher λ makes grokking near-universal and shortens the gap more than tenfold (r9, r10, r11). Norms fall to a median 0.42 of their Tmem value by generalization in all 14 runs (r12). This is consistent with a low-norm bias; circuit efficiency was not tested.
relationships.display_finding: Higher λ made grokking nearly universal and shortened the delay more than tenfold, while norms declined by generalization to a median 0.42 of their value at memorization across all 14 runs.
